components.name: card header
components.description:
What the Component Does
Provides the title area for the main card component, with optional leading/trailing icons and a subtitle where supported. Its primary use is to identify the card’s content and provide relevant header affordances while keeping the card’s heading consistent.

This is a supporting component for the main card’s header slot. Usage is restricted to the main card component; it is not a standalone page, container, dialog, or specialized-card header.

Variants and Controls
• Property 1=center-header: the default centered-header presentation, with title and optional icons in a horizontal row.
• Property 1=left-header: a left-aligned header presentation with an optional subtitle beneath the title row.
• Title sm: controls visibility of the small-title presentation; default is false.
• title lg: controls visibility of the large-title presentation; default is true. Use one title presentation at a time rather than showing both.
• right icon: controls the trailing icon; default is true.
• left icon: controls the leading icon; default is false.
• has subtitle: controls the subtitle in the left-header presentation; default is false. The center-header variant contains no subtitle presentation.
• Replace “Card Title” and “Card subtitle” with meaningful content through the relevant text layers. Title and subtitle text are not exposed as component-level text properties.
• The default icon artwork is sample content, not a prescribed action. Choose icons that accurately represent the associated content or action.
• This set exposes visibility controls rather than content slots. It is intended to be supplied within the main card’s header slot.
• The two variants define header composition, not hover, selected, or interaction states. Any icon actions and accessible labeling must be configured in implementation.

Use Cases and Exceptions
Recommended usage:
• Use only as the header of the main card component. Select center-header or left-header according to the card’s content hierarchy and applicable product rules.
• Write a concise, descriptive title that identifies the card’s subject. Keep the title consistent with the body content.
• Use a subtitle only in left-header when supporting context is necessary; do not repeat the title or place lengthy body content in the subtitle.
• Choose the appropriate title presentation for the parent card and show only that title. Keep text readable without colliding with icons.
• Hide optional icons when they provide no meaningful information or action. Give interactive icons accessible names and keyboard access in implementation.
• Let the parent card govern the surrounding header, content, and action layout. Do not repurpose this component to bypass another component’s own header structure.

Exceptions:
• Scope restriction: this component is permitted only within the main card component’s header slot. Do not use it independently or in unrelated components.
• Subtitle support is limited to left-header; do not assume the center-header variant supports it.
• No exception to the main-card-only usage restriction is defined.

components.name: card
components.description:
What the Component Does?

Groups related content and its supporting actions into a distinct surface.

Its primary use is to present one coherent topic, record, summary, or task with a header, body, and optional call-to-action area, making the content easy to scan within a larger page.

Variants and Controls

• Type=elevated: a card presentation for visually separating content from its surrounding surface. Supports status=Default, hover, and banner.
• Type=tonal: an alternate surface treatment for grouped content. Supports status=Default only.

• type=small: a compact card presentation. Supports status=Default and hover.

• status=Default: resting presentation.

• status=hover: pointer-over presentation; it does not establish that the entire card is clickable.

• status=banner: a distinct header/banner presentation, not an interaction state. Available only for elevated cards.

• primary color: a variant axis with values true and false, available for each supported type/status combination. Use the matching color treatment for the surrounding design; this is a variant selector, not a Boolean visibility control.

• The set contains 12 variants, not every possible combination of its axes. Current Figma default: type=elevated, status=Default, primary color=true.

Content controls:

• header slot: supplies the card header. Default and hover samples contain a nested card header; banner samples use a different header composition.

• content Slot: supplies the main body; empty in the sample variants. Populate it with the card’s meaningful content.

• CTA slot: supplies the action area; empty in the sample variants.

• has CTA: shows or hides the CTA slot; default is true. Hide it when the card has no actions.
• has header: defaults to true, but its visibility binding is currently present only on the small variants. Do not rely on it to hide headers on elevated or tonal variants.

• The card stacks header, body, and actions vertically. Text and controls inside supplied content are configured through that content, not card-level text properties.

• Navigation, header actions, hover behavior, and responsive sizing must be configured in implementation; this set does not define those behaviors.

Use Cases and Exceptions

• Use elevated for summaries or task-focused content that needs clear separation from the page.

• Use tonal when an alternate surface treatment fits the page hierarchy; do not assume hover or banner combinations exist for this type.

• Use small for concise content in compact layouts. Use a larger card when the content needs more reading space rather than crowding the compact presentation.

• Use banner when the card needs a distinct header treatment. Keep the banner’s title and content consistent with the body.

• Keep one coherent subject per card, use a descriptive heading, and include only actions related to that subject.

• Distinguish whole-card navigation from buttons or other controls inside the card. Do not imply clickability solely through hover styling.

• Follow the button family’s hierarchy and size guidance for actions placed in the CTA slot.

• Use a list or table instead when users need dense scanning or aligned comparison across many records.

• In implementation, preserve readable content, visible keyboard focus for interactive elements, and accessible names for icon-only header actions.

components.name: card-container
components.description:
What the Component Does
Provides a collapsible card shell with a section header and optional body content. Use type=collapsed for the header-only state and type=expand for the open state. Choose style=data tile for structured metric content or style=free content for approved custom content. Set status to Default or hover, swap the header icon as needed, and use the multiple values and single values properties to control supported data-tile arrangements. Insert approved content through the content and Section Header slots.


Use Cases
• Grouping related dashboard metrics inside an expandable section.
• Reducing page density by showing a summary before revealing details.
• Presenting single-value or multi-value data tiles in a shared container.
• Hosting custom section content with the free content style.
• Showing hover feedback for an interactive card header.


Exceptions

components.name: Header
components.description:
What the Component Does
Provides the application’s top header, bringing together platform branding, a menu icon, and the user’s avatar-menu access point. Its primary use is to maintain a consistent application shell while exposing relevant top-level controls. The Taxonomy presentation additionally includes a search area.

This is the application header, not a content-card header. Platform navigation remains in the left-hand menu, and account/help/preferences content is supplied through the avatar menu.

Variants and Controls
• Version=Default: the default presentation, containing the Business@Slalom branding, menu icon, and nested avatar menu.
• Version=Taxonomy: contains the branding and menu icon, plus a Function Group with a Search presentation and nested avatar menu.
• Version is the only exposed Header property. There are no header-level text properties, visibility switches, content slots, or responsive/open-state variants.
• Both nested avatar menus use status=Default in the samples. Configure their identity information, content slots, and opened/closed presentation through the avatar menu component, following its documented application-specific guidance.
• The menu element is an icon instance, not the contextual action-menu component. Its presence does not establish a navigation-expansion interaction.
• Search in Version=Taxonomy is a frame containing a search icon and “Search” text. It is a visual presentation, not a functioning text input or an exposed Header search property.
• Branding is supplied as artwork. Preserve the approved branding rather than editing it as a generic page title.
• The header uses a horizontal layout. Sample dimensions do not define breakpoint behavior, sticky positioning, or automatic rearrangement.
• Menu activation, avatar-menu behavior, search input/results, navigation, and responsive adaptation must be configured in implementation. The variants alone do not provide those behaviors.

Use Cases and Exceptions
Recommended usage:
• Use at the top of the application layout for consistent branding and access to shell-level controls.
• Use Default for the standard header composition and Taxonomy for the Taxonomy context requiring its search presentation, according to product rules.
• Keep the header distinct from page titles, breadcrumbs, and local action groups. Do not move unrelated card or table commands into it.
• Coordinate the menu icon with the approved left-navigation behavior; do not define a different navigation system solely through this header.
• Configure the avatar menu for the current application, retaining its approved identity, help, preferences, policy, and footer content where applicable.
• For Taxonomy search, define the supported search scope, input behavior, and results experience explicitly. Replace a static presentation with an accessible implementation rather than treating the sample as functional.
• Check available width so branding, search, and avatar controls remain readable and do not collide. Follow product guidance for smaller breakpoints; no separate mobile or tablet variant is supplied.
• In implementation, provide accessible names, keyboard access, and visible focus for interactive controls. Give search a clear label and the avatar activator an appropriate expanded-state indication.

Exceptions:
• the search taxonomy version is not a approved version yet, so for now the standar version is the only allowed version.
• Avatar-menu content and behavior are governed by the avatar menu component, not Header-level variants.
• No alternative positioning, sticky behavior, or breakpoint-specific exception is defined by this set; follow product-specific guidance.

components.name: content-slot
components.description:
What the Component Does
Provides the descriptive body text for the main card component. Its primary use is to explain the card’s subject or supply supporting information between the header and any related actions, using a consistent centered or left-aligned presentation.

Usage is restricted to the main card component’s content area. Despite its name, content-slot is a component set containing text, not an exposed content slot for arbitrary inserted content.

Variants and Controls
• type=content-centered: the default variant; the visible body text is center-aligned.
• type=content-left: the visible body text is left-aligned. Select based on the parent card’s content hierarchy and product rules.
• type is the only exposed property. There are no top-level text, visibility, instance-swap, or content-slot controls.
• Both variants contain a visible text layer named Subtitle with placeholder body copy. Replace its content through the relevant text layer; the layer name does not make it the card header’s subtitle.
• The visible body text uses truncation in a fixed sample area. Longer copy may be clipped or truncated; do not assume automatic height growth or an included Read More action.
• Each variant also contains a hidden Description-left frame. It is not a separate exposed control and is not the visible text source; do not populate hidden content instead of the active text.
• The variant names describe text alignment. The visible frame is named Description-Centered in both variants, but the visible text alignment differs correctly.
• No hover, selected, loading, expansion, or scrolling states are provided. Any expanded reading experience must be defined through the parent card and implementation.

Use Cases and Exceptions
Recommended usage:
• Use only as descriptive body content within the main card component’s content Slot.
• Keep copy relevant to the card’s title and purpose. Replace placeholder text with concise, accurate information.
• Use content-centered for centered card compositions and content-left when left alignment suits the surrounding content and reading needs.
• Check the final copy at the intended card width. Preserve readability and avoid collisions with the card header or CTA area.
• Do not rely on truncated text as the only source of essential instructions or information. If full copy is necessary, provide a product-approved accessible way to read it or choose an appropriate content composition for the main card.
• Keep card actions in the parent card’s CTA area rather than treating this text component as an action group.
• Do not use this component to host forms, tables, tab panels, or other arbitrary content; it exposes text-alignment variants, not a general content insertion slot.

Exceptions:
• Scope restriction: this component is permitted only within the main card component. Do not use it independently, in other components, or in specialized cards.
• Long content requires explicit handling because the visible text presentation truncates; no built-in expansion behavior is supplied.
• No exception to the main-card-only usage restriction is defined.

components.name: cards/digitalexperts
components.description:
What the Component Does
Presents a Digital Expert or Prompt Library entry with its title, purpose, supporting information, and contextual actions so users can scan available content and take the appropriate action.

This is a specialized card family with strict section boundaries. The digital-experts type is only for the Digital Experts section’s “Slalom Digital Experts”, “My Digital Experts”, and “Digital Experts Shared with Me” tabs. The prompt-library type is only for the Prompt Library section.

Variants and Controls
• type=digital-experts: presents an expert image, title, description, creator/model information, and “Launch Expert” action.
• type=prompt-library: presents a prompt title, description, and category tags. Do not assume it shares the Digital Expert launch action.
• Both types support status=default, hover-card, hover-cta, and menu-pressed.
• default: resting presentation. Current Figma default is type=digital-experts, status=default.
• hover-card: card-hover presentation.
• hover-cta: CTA-hover presentation; the Prompt Library samples have a hidden button container, so this status does not establish a visible launch button for that type.
• menu-pressed: open contextual-menu presentation. The Digital Expert sample includes “Create Smart Link”, “Manage Access”, “Edit”, and “Delete”. The Prompt Library sample includes “Edit” and “Delete”; sample visibility does not grant permission.
• Digital Experts additionally support description expanded (longer description with “Close Description”), banner (sample “Recently Added” header), and saving files (file-saving feedback). These statuses are not available for prompt-library.
• The set contains 11 variants, not every possible type/status combination.
• banner icon and info section are Boolean controls that default to true; Helper text defaults to false. Their current visibility bindings are in the digital-experts / saving files variant, not across every card status.
• Titles, descriptions, tags, creator/model information, imagery, and menu labels are configured through the relevant card content; there are no equivalent top-level text properties or content slots exposed by this set.
• Launching, description expansion, menu opening, file-saving progress, and action authorization must be implemented separately. The variants are visual presentations, not permission enforcement.

Use Cases and Exceptions
Required usage:
• Slalom Digital Experts: use digital-experts cards; the only permitted contextual-menu action is “Create Smart Link”. Do not expose Manage Access, Edit, or Delete.
• Digital Experts Shared with Me: use digital-experts cards; the only permitted contextual-menu action is “Create Smart Link”. Do not expose Manage Access, Edit, or Delete.
• My Digital Experts: use digital-experts cards and allow the full defined menu: “Create Smart Link”, “Manage Access”, “Edit”, and “Delete”.
• Apply these restrictions to contextual-menu actions. They do not remove the card’s separate “Launch Expert” action.
• Prompt Library: use prompt-library cards only in that section. Configure its actions according to Prompt Library permission rules; do not transfer the My Digital Experts exception to prompt cards.
• Keep titles, descriptions, imagery, and tags accurate for the represented entry. Do not treat sample model names, creator text, banner labels, or file counts as universal values.
• Use expanded descriptions for fuller context and saving files only for actual file-saving progress. Keep counts and readiness feedback consistent with the real process.
• Ensure the menu shows only actions allowed for the current tab, and enforce the same restrictions in implementation. Do not rely on the full sample menu as an authorization source.
• Provide accessible names and keyboard access for menu controls, launch actions, and description expansion. Use the applicable confirmation flow for destructive actions.

Exceptions:
• My Digital Experts is the only exception to the Create Smart Link-only Digital Expert menu rule: all four defined menu options are permitted there.
• No exception allows the digital-experts type outside the three named Digital Experts tabs.
• No exception allows the prompt-library type outside the Prompt Library section.

components.name: bottom sheet
components.description:
What the Component Does
Provides a dialog-style surface that elevates content above the current page from the bottom of the screen. Its primary use is to present contextual content or a focused interaction without navigating away from the current view.

Vuetify describes a bottom sheet as a modified dialog that slides from the bottom. Unlike bottom navigation, which contains buttons and application-level navigation actions, a bottom sheet can contain varied content.


Variants and Controls
• type=desktop: the default layout presentation for desktop breakpoints.

• type=tablet: the layout presentation for tablet 
breakpoints; do not treat it as the mobile variant.

• type=mobile: the layout presentation for mobile breakpoints.

• Content Slot: the single exposed slot in all three variants. Populate it with the sheet’s meaningful content; it is empty in every sample.

• All variants use a vertical layout. There are no separate header, action-footer, close-icon, or open/closed controls exposed by this set. 


Add any required title, actions, and dismissal affordance within the supplied content.

• The variants are presentation choices, not automatic breakpoint switching or working overlay behavior. Opening, dismissal, focus management, scrolling, and positioning must be configured in implementation.

• Vuetify recommends cards, lists, or sheets as content containers inside a bottom sheet. Use the corresponding design-system components rather than assuming the empty Content Slot supplies their structure.
• Vuetify supports controlling visibility through v-model/model-value or an activator slot. An activator slot is not required when visibility is controlled by the model. These are implementation options, not properties exposed by this Figma set.
• Vuetify’s optional inset mode limits desktop content width to 70%; width can reduce it further. This is an optional implementation treatment, not a mandatory width or a dedicated variant in this set. Follow product rules when selecting it.

Use Cases and Exceptions

• Present contextual lists of actions or destinations, such as an “Open in” chooser, using a list inside Content Slot.

• Present a focused content experience, such as a compact media player, using a card or sheet inside Content Slot.

• Keep the content related to the current task and provide a clear title or context when needed.
• Choose desktop, tablet, or mobile according to the active product breakpoint. Adapt to the available viewport and define internal scrolling when content would otherwise be clipped.

• Provide a clear, accessible way to dismiss or complete the interaction. In implementation, apply dialog focus management, keyboard access, and a task-appropriate Escape/outside-click policy.

• Do not substitute a bottom sheet for persistent bottom navigation. Use bottom navigation for application-level navigation rather than an overlay containing that navigation.

• Use a dedicated page or another approved surface when a lengthy workflow cannot remain readable and usable within the sheet.

Exceptions:
• Inset desktop sizing is optional; do not apply its 70% width rule to tablet or mobile without product-specific guidance.

• Do not automatically inherit the drawer’s 90% desktop width, mobile sizing rules, fixed footer, or prescribed button arrangement. 


This is a separate component; any such requirement must be explicitly defined for its use case.

• Additional restrictions or exceptions require product-specific guidance.

components.name: container
components.description:
What the Component Does?

Provides the base layout surface for page content sections. Use containers to group related section content consistently and follow the applicable product’s layout rules for placement, arrangement, and content composition.


Standard content inside containers must maintain 32 px padding for consistency. The minimum container width is 460 px, corresponding to the minimum breakpoint. 

Do not reduce the container below this width or reduce standard content padding to fit a narrower layout.

Variants and Controls
• type=general container: the default variant for content sections without an embedded table. The container has 32 px padding on all four sides and a minimum width of 460 px.

• type=table container: the table-specific version referred to in product guidance as Type B. Select this variant whenever a container includes a table.

• header: a content slot available in both variants. In general container, it is the available slot for section content; in table container, use it for the heading, controls, or other content above the table.

• Table slot: available only in table container. Insert the table here, not inside the padded header area. This slot has 0 px padding on all sides.

• Both variants use a vertical layout and have a 460 px minimum width. The sample width is 1400 px, not a required usage width.

• Current table-container spacing: the outer frame has 32 px top, 0 px side, and 16 px bottom padding; its header supplies 32 px left/right padding. These observed values distinguish the table region from standard padded content; the Table slot itself remains unpadded.

• Both slots are empty in the samples. Populate them with the intended section content. No text, interaction, or breakpoint-switching controls are exposed at container level.

Use Cases and Exceptions

• Use containers as the foundation for page content sections, following the product’s page-layout rules rather than treating each section as an unrelated surface.

• Choose general container for non-table section content and keep the standard 32 px content inset. Avoid adding a second 32 px outer inset inside the already padded container.

• Choose Type B / table container whenever the section includes a table. Keep non-table content aligned to the standard 32 px inset while placing the table directly in Table slot.

• Preserve the 460 px minimum width when arranging containers across breakpoints. Define any narrower-screen adaptation through product layout guidance; do not invent a smaller container breakpoint.

• Ensure inserted content fits without clipping or overlapping. Configure table overflow and responsive behavior according to product rules rather than changing the container’s padding or minimum width.

Exceptions:
• Table content is the explicit padding exception: use the Type B / table container variant and keep the table section at 0 px padding. Do not apply the standard 32 px inset to the table region.
• Additional exceptions require product-specific guidance.

• The menu element is an icon instance, not the contextual action-menu component. Its presence does not establish a navigation-expansion interaction.
• Search in Version=Taxonomy is a frame containing a search icon and “Search” text. It is a visual presentation, not a functioning text input or an exposed Header search property.
• Branding is supplied as artwork. Preserve the approved branding rather than editing it as a generic page title.
• The header uses a horizontal layout. Sample dimensions do not define breakpoint behavior, sticky positioning, or automatic rearrangement.
• Menu activation, avatar-menu behavior, search input/results, navigation, and responsive adaptation must be configured in implementation. The variants alone do not provide those behaviors.

Use Cases and Exceptions
Recommended usage:
• Use at the top of the application layout for consistent branding and access to shell-level controls.
• Use Default for the standard header composition and Taxonomy for the Taxonomy context requiring its search presentation, according to product rules.
• Keep the header distinct from page titles, breadcrumbs, and local action groups. Do not move unrelated card or table commands into it.
• Coordinate the menu icon with the approved left-navigation behavior; do not define a different navigation system solely through this header.
• Configure the avatar menu for the current application, retaining its approved identity, help, preferences, policy, and footer content where applicable.
• For Taxonomy search, define the supported search scope, input behavior, and results experience explicitly. Replace a static presentation with an accessible implementation rather than treating the sample as functional.
• Check available width so branding, search, and avatar controls remain readable and do not collide. Follow product guidance for smaller breakpoints; no separate mobile or tablet variant is supplied.
• In implementation, provide accessible names, keyboard access, and visible focus for interactive controls. Give search a clear label and the avatar activator an appropriate expanded-state indication.

Exceptions:
• the search taxonomy version is not a approved version yet, so for now the standar version is the only allowed version.
• Avatar-menu content and behavior are governed by the avatar menu component, not Header-level variants.
• No alternative positioning, sticky behavior, or breakpoint-specific exception is defined by this set; follow product-specific guidance.

components.name: card header
components.description:
What the Component Does
Provides the title area for the main card component, with optional leading/trailing icons and a subtitle where supported. Its primary use is to identify the card’s content and provide relevant header affordances while keeping the card’s heading consistent.

This is a supporting component for the main card’s header slot. Usage is restricted to the main card component; it is not a standalone page, container, dialog, or specialized-card header.

Variants and Controls
• Property 1=center-header: the default centered-header presentation, with title and optional icons in a horizontal row.
• Property 1=left-header: a left-aligned header presentation with an optional subtitle beneath the title row.
• Title sm: controls visibility of the small-title presentation; default is false.
• title lg: controls visibility of the large-title presentation; default is true. Use one title presentation at a time rather than showing both.
• right icon: controls the trailing icon; default is true.
• left icon: controls the leading icon; default is false.
• has subtitle: controls the subtitle in the left-header presentation; default is false. The center-header variant contains no subtitle presentation.
• Replace “Card Title” and “Card subtitle” with meaningful content through the relevant text layers. Title and subtitle text are not exposed as component-level text properties.
• The default icon artwork is sample content, not a prescribed action. Choose icons that accurately represent the associated content or action.
• This set exposes visibility controls rather than content slots. It is intended to be supplied within the main card’s header slot.
• The two variants define header composition, not hover, selected, or interaction states. Any icon actions and accessible labeling must be configured in implementation.

Use Cases and Exceptions
Recommended usage:
• Use only as the header of the main card component. Select center-header or left-header according to the card’s content hierarchy and applicable product rules.
• Write a concise, descriptive title that identifies the card’s subject. Keep the title consistent with the body content.
• Use a subtitle only in left-header when supporting context is necessary; do not repeat the title or place lengthy body content in the subtitle.
• Choose the appropriate title presentation for the parent card and show only that title. Keep text readable without colliding with icons.
• Hide optional icons when they provide no meaningful information or action. Give interactive icons accessible names and keyboard access in implementation.
• Let the parent card govern the surrounding header, content, and action layout. Do not repurpose this component to bypass another component’s own header structure.

Exceptions:
• Scope restriction: this component is permitted only within the main card component’s header slot. Do not use it independently or in unrelated components.
• Subtitle support is limited to left-header; do not assume the center-header variant supports it.
• No exception to the main-card-only usage restriction is defined.

components.name: drawer
components.description:
What the Component Does
Provides a focused surface for contextual information, data entry, or a system task while retaining the surrounding page context. 


The drawer separates a header, central content area, and bottom action area so users can access the full content without losing the main actions.

Required responsive behavior:

• Desktop: use size=desktop only at desktop breakpoints. Drawer width must be 90% of the current viewport width at the active desktop breakpoint and adapt as the viewport changes; do not hard-code the sample width.

• Tablet: use size=tablet at tablet breakpoints, following the product’s tablet layout rules. Tablet is a separate presentation, not a mobile layout; mobile’s full-width and bottom-overlay restrictions do not apply.

• Mobile: use size=mobile at mobile breakpoints. Drawer width must be 100% of the viewport, with a bottom-anchored presentation that overlays the page to the bottom edge.

• For long content, allow only the central internal content area to scroll vertically. Keep the drawer within the available viewport rather than growing the entire surface beyond it.

Variants and Controls

• size: desktop, tablet, mobile. The default variant is desktop. These variants define layout presentations, not open/closed states.

• size=tablet: use at tablet breakpoints with tablet-specific sizing and placement according to product rules. 


Do not apply mobile’s 100% width or bottom-anchored overlay rule to tablet. 


Tablet may also be used on desktop only under the documented limited-content exception. 


Tablet width percentages and breakpoint thresholds are not specified here.

• header: supplies the drawer heading and any relevant header content.

• content: supplies the central body. Use this as the vertically scrollable region when content exceeds the available height.

• button set: supplies the bottom action area. Keep this area fixed at the bottom of the drawer and outside the scrolling content so the main CTAs remain visible.

• has CTA Section: controls button set visibility and defaults to true. Required usage keeps it true; do not hide the action area for the drawer experience described here.

• All three slots are empty in the samples. Populate them with the intended heading, content, and actions.

• Sample dimensions are not fixed usage dimensions. Responsive widths, bottom anchoring, scrolling, fixed footer behavior, dismissal, and task actions must be configured in implementation; the presence of slots alone does not establish these behaviors.

Use Cases and Exceptions

• Use for a contextual task or information flow that benefits from an overlay while maintaining page context.

• Populate the header with a clear title and the central content with one coherent task or topic.

• Keep the button set at the bottom and fixed throughout the experience, including when central content is long or scrolled.

• Place the main action on the right using a contained button (contained_button), size=md.

• Place Exit or Cancel on the left using a neutral outlined button (neutral_outlined), size=md. All buttons in the drawer action area must be md.

• When content grows, expand its internal scrollable content extent, not the full drawer height. Reserve visible space for the footer so it never covers the final content or scrolls out of reach.

• Preserve 90% responsive width for size=desktop and 100% for size=mobile. Use size=tablet on desktop only under the documented exception. Use the product’s breakpoint definitions; no numeric breakpoint thresholds are supplied by this component guidance.

• In implementation, provide clear action labels, keyboard access, visible focus, and a dismissal policy appropriate to unsaved data. For a modal overlay, manage focus within the drawer and restore it to the trigger on dismissal.

Exceptions:

• Desktop exception: size=tablet may be used at desktop breakpoints only when the drawer content is not large and the information behind the drawer needs to remain visible. 

Use size=desktop with its 90% responsive width for other desktop cases. This exception does not change the fixed bottom action area, md button sizing, or central-only vertical scrolling.

• This drawer’s required action pattern explicitly pairs a right-side contained primary action with a left-side neutral outlined Exit/Cancel action. Apply this drawer-specific pattern even where general button guidance reserves contained buttons for standalone actions.

• Tablet responsive sizing requires product-specific guidance. No exception to the fixed bottom actions, md button sizing, or central-only scrolling is defined.

components.name: modal
components.description:
What the Component Does?

Presents focused information, a decision, or a task in a dialog without requiring users to leave the current product context. 
Use dialogs to ensure users understand relevant product information, respond to important warnings or urgent decisions, or enter data and perform system-related tasks.


Variants and Controls

• type=alert: informs users about important warnings or decisions requiring urgent attention. Keep the message and response focused on the immediate issue.

• type=data: supports information and knowledge introduction, including data definitions, terminology, tutorials, and guidance; also supports relevant data entry and task workflows that need more content space.

• type=announcement: highlights relevant launches or information users need to know, such as policies or new features. Uses a distinct banner-style header.

• rounded corner: a variant axis with values true and false. The set contains both treatments, but permitted usage is restricted to rounded corner=true for alert, data, and announcement. 

Use a 24 px corner radius (radius-xl) and 24 px dialog content padding on all sides (pa-6). 

The 24 px radius is corner rounding, not border stroke thickness. Do not use rounded corner=false or override these radius and padding values.


• Current Figma default: type=alert, rounded corner=true.

• content slot: supplies the dialog body. Insert the relevant information, warning, form, or task content; sample bodies are empty.

• CTA Section: supplies response or task actions; empty in the samples.

• Show CTA Section: shows or hides the action section in all three types; default is true.

• close: shows or hides the trailing close icon in alert and data variants; default is true. 

Announcement variants have no close icon bound to this control, so it does not provide announcement dismissal.

• has icon: shows or hides the leading header icon in alert and data variants; default is true. It is not bound to an icon in announcement variants.

• upper case and Sentence Case: control alternative title text visibility in data variants; defaults are false and true respectively. Show one title presentation at a time and supply the correct title wording. 

These controls are not general text-case controls for every dialog type.

• Titles are not exposed as component-level text properties. Replace sample header titles through the appropriate text content.

• The dialog organizes header, body, and action content vertically. Sample dimensions are not documented responsive breakpoint rules.

• Backdrop, opening, dismissal, focus handling, validation, submission, and scrolling must be configured separately in implementation; this set contains no open/closed or persistent-dialog variants.

Use Cases and Exceptions

• Use only the rounded-corner version: rounded corner=true, 24 px corner radius (radius-xl), and 24 px padding (pa-6). Apply this rule to every dialog type, regardless of its informational, warning, announcement, or task purpose.

Recommended usage:
• Product information: use data for definitions, terminology, tutorials, or guidance; use announcement when a policy, legal update, launch, or new feature needs prominent awareness. Choose based on the purpose, not merely the amount of text.

• Urgent warnings or decisions: use alert. State the issue, consequence, and required decision clearly; give response actions explicit labels.

• Data entry and system tasks: use data. Include clear field labels, relevant instructions, validation feedback, and actions appropriate to completing or cancelling the task.

• Populate content slot and CTA Section with a coherent task or message. Hide an unused CTA section only when another clear dismissal or completion route exists.

• Follow the button family’s hierarchy and size rules. Contained actions are for standalone highest emphasis; for three-action modals or alerts, a negative outlined md button may serve as the second-hierarchy action.

• Provide a clear, product-approved dismissal route. Hiding a close icon does not make a dialog persistent, and critical decisions must not be accidentally bypassed by an unspecified dismissal behavior.

• In implementation, give the dialog an accessible title, move focus into it, contain keyboard focus while modal, and restore focus to the trigger on dismissal. Define Escape and outside-click behavior according to the task and unsaved-data requirements.

• Keep content readable within the available viewport and define scrolling for long content. Use a dedicated page for lengthy or complex workflows that do not need a dialog.

• Avoid interrupting users with a dialog for routine information that can remain inline, and avoid stacking dialogs for unrelated tasks.

Exceptions:

• Announcement does not expose the same close-icon and leading-icon behavior as alert and data; provide any required dismissal through an explicit action or approved surrounding behavior.

• No exception to the required rounded version, 24 px radius (radius-xl), or 24 px padding (pa-6) is defined. Any exception requires explicit product approval.
